entities.summary: Written c. 116 CE by the Roman senator and historian Tacitus, the Annals cover the reigns of Tiberius, Caligula, Claudius, and Nero (14–68 CE). Written with devastating concision and psychological insight, they are the primary source for early imperial Rome. Tacitus's portrait of tyranny's corrosion of public virtue has influenced every subsequent generation of political writers, from Machiavelli to the American Founders.
